title: The State and Revolution
author: Vladimir Lenin
current_text: In 1940 an Oklahoma City police detective bought copies of Lenin's The State and Revolution at a bookstore. Police then raided the store and seized more than 10,000 books.

sources.quote: On July 24, 1940, an Oklahoma City police detective dressed as an oil field worker walked into the bookstore, and purchased copies of: ” Vladimir Lenin’s “The State and Revolution,”
sources.title: Oklahoma Gazette: Bookstore arrests of the forties presaged communist scare

sources.quote: On Aug. 17, police raided the store, arresting about 20 people ” including customers ” and seized more than 10,000 books.
sources.title: Oklahoma Gazette: Bookstore arrests of the forties presaged communist scare

ban_rows.note: Seized as obscene in Boston in 1927; in a 1940 Oklahoma City raid copies were seized and burned along with the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution (convictions reversed on appeal in 1943).
Banned in Malaysia by the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) under the Printing Presses and Publications Act. Gazetted 1952-06-12 (L.N. 329). Publisher: LITTLE LENIN LIBRARY. Language: INGGERIS.

Wikipedia's list records this title as prohibited under Singapore's Internal Security (Prohibition of Publications) (Consolidation) Order (G.N. S 413/1950, extended to Singapore in 1963). The date the title was prohibited and any lifting could not be verified.
